entries.subject: Native Band 6 continuum image
entries.finding: The public CASA 4.2.2 science-verification FITS reference image is obtainable and retains its original WCS, units and restoring beam. Its peak and noise agree with the published measurements.
The published eight-ring ellipse fit provides the common plane. The full native radial profile supplies the rings and gaps; depth remains inferred.
Use a constant 1 au Gaussian approximation anchored to Pinte et al.’s settled millimeter dust near 100 au, with the simplification stated. Do not use the gas’s 10 au scale height.

The initial one-belt fit reached its radial-width boundary at 0.6 of the reference radius. The image contains multiple rings. Keep this Gaussian as a baseline and require the measured-profile disc to beat it, the shell and constant depth.
entries.revisitWhen: A distinct single-belt dataset is selected.

entries.finding: Decode the 256 underlying vector colors without tick strokes and calibrate the nonlinear flux axis with the nine printed ticks. Two held-out ticks validate the recovered display power near 0.55. The positive 2-rms lower endpoint is supported by the actual ticks despite the caption’s negative sign.

Opacity taken from the displayed color made the gap near 64 au, 4% of the top of the scale, 62% opaque, with a median line of sight at 0.64. Opacity now follows the measured brightness and the column keeps the scale’s hue; the median line of sight is 0.11.
The 2014 release also provides a resolved 0.87 mm continuum image. The selected 1.3 mm view already supplies the requested ring scene and matches the adopted millimeter-dust prior.

Guerra-Alvarado et al. (2024), A&A 686, A298, resolves 0.45 mm emission at 2 au and discusses a thicker inner emitting layer. It is a different tracer and is not substituted for the settled 1.3 mm dust.
entries.revisitWhen: Its own native image and wavelength-specific vertical model are selected for a separate dataset.
